veranderings.blok: Wanneer 'n kind se regte geskend word
veranderings.voor: speel nie en die rede hou nie.
veranderings.na: speel nie, en die rede hou nie steek nie.
veranderings.rede: The Afrikaans idiom is 'hou nie steek nie' ('hou nie' alone echoes English 'does not hold'), and two clauses with their own subject and verb take an AWS comma before 'en'.

veranderings.blok: Wanneer 'n kind se regte geskend word
veranderings.rede: 'ophou' can be read as 'stop', while 'vertraag' clearly means 'hold up', which is what the sentence intends.

veranderings.voor: dag en nag oop en iemand
veranderings.na: dag en nag oop, en iemand
veranderings.rede: AWS comma: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.

veranderings.voor: om te vertel en die grootmense
veranderings.na: om te vertel, en die grootmense
veranderings.rede: AWS comma: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb ('Jou werk is' / 'die grootmense se werk is').
People make a plan rather than do it, and this matches the block heading.

veranderings.voor: Eers sien die nuwe seun se klas raak
veranderings.na: Eers sien die nuwe seun se klas dit raak
veranderings.rede: The separable verb 'raaksien' needs an object here; without 'dit' the sentence can be misread as an instruction to notice the class.

veranderings.blok: Wie wat doen in die plan
veranderings.rede: 'vertel' takes 'vir' for the person told, as elsewhere in the lesson; 'by wie' is the wrong preposition.

vlae.teks: Sê dat dit gebeur en bly naby die ander kinders.
vlae.rede: Vague: it does not say to whom the child should say it, nor which 'other children' to stay near (the excluded child, or friends for safety); it cannot be clarified without guessing the intended content, so it is flagged rather than changed.
